BILL NUMBER:  S3834

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public health law, in relation to exemption of
certain damages recovered by or on behalf of patients of residential
health care facilities


 PURPOSE :
To exempt damages that have been awarded to nursing home patients or
to their representative or estate from collection by Medicaid.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Current law says that if a nursing home patient is awarded monetary
damages to compensate for injury by a nursing home, that award shall
not be subject to a Medicaid lien to pay for benefits or counted
towards eligibility. This bill would amend section 2801-d(5) of the
Public Health Law to make it clear that this exemption applies to
payment of past and future medical care and add a patient's legal
representative and estate to the protected parties.

 EXISTING LAW :
None.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Following the 1975 massive scandal of fraud and abuse in nursing
homes, Public Health Law § 2801-d was enacted to give patients
increased powers to enforce their right to adequate treatment and care
by providing them the right to sue for damages and other relief.

The law says that if a nursing home patient is awarded monetary
damages to compensate for injury by a nursing home, that award shall
not be subject to a Medicaid lien to pay for benefits or counted
towards eligibility. However, it does not specifically address the
situation that may arise if a patient dies before the conclusion of
the case.

The principle of the law is designed not only to be fair but also to
encourage patients to do the extensive work necessary to bring a
successful lawsuit. The law should be clear that this exemption
applies even if the patient dies and the claim is brought by the
patient's legal representative or estate.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to: (a)
hospital inpatient discharges on or after the first of April after it
shall have become a law; and (b) other services provided on or after
the first of April after it shall have become a law.

summary: Provides a clarification of the exemption of certain damages recovered by or on behalf of patients of residential health care facilities.
